recommended_model: Nutri-Score, updated algorithm (Scientific Committee update for solid foods, voted 29 Jun 2022 and adopted 26 Jul 2022; beverages update, voted 1 Feb 2023 and adopted 30 Mar 2023). Use its three algorithms: general foods (with the cheese and red-meat rules), fats/oils/nuts/seeds, and beverages. The fruit/vegetable/legume (FVL) component defaults to 0 points. Shown next to it, as an India-specific flag that is not part of the score: the WHO SEARO 2017 nutrient-profile pass/fail and the FSSAI 2022-draft 'HFSS' test.
why: 1) It is the only candidate that is graded (A–E from a continuous point total), category-specific (3 algorithms + cheese/red-meat rules), fully published with exact point tables, scientifically reviewed (and re-calibrated in 2022/2023 against EU food-composition databases), and in force as a public FOP scheme (FR, BE, DE, LU, NL, ES, CH; the updated algorithm has been in use since 2024 with transition periods). 2) It can be calculated from the data we already have: energy, total sugars, saturated fat, sodium (as salt ×2.5), fibre, protein, and total fat (for the fats ratio). Only FVL% is missing. Since the 2022 update that matters less, because the old 'protein counts when N≥11 if FVL=5' exception was removed (only cheese keeps it), so FVL no longer changes whether protein counts. 3) The India-specific alternatives are not usable as a score. FSSAI's Indian Nutrition Rating (INR) was only ever a 2022 draft, was never notified, and has since been effectively set aside in favour of warning labels. It also needs fruit/veg AND nuts/legumes/millets % (we have neither) and gives 0 points to dairy, ghee, oils, flour, sweeteners etc. (exempted). The WHO SEARO model is pass/fail for marketing to children with no grade, and many categories have only 1–2 thresholds. 4) Health Star Rating is graded and well documented, but it is an Australia/NZ scheme. Like Nutri-Score it needs FVNL%, and it has no special handling of oils by fatty-acid profile (Nutri-Score's sat/total-fat ratio is useful for Indian oils such as mustard, groundnut, rice-bran, coconut and palm, and for ghee/vanaspati). The FSSAI 2022 INR draft itself was 'based on the Health Star Rating'. Nutri-Score is graded and public, but it has no standing in Indian regulation. So, in shopper text, call it 'the European Nutri-Score method', never an Indian or FSSAI rating.
threshold_convention: Unless noted, arrays are inclusive upper bounds: points = number of thresholds t with value > t, i.e. value ≤ arr[0] → 0 points, ≤ arr[1] → 1 point, …, > arr[-1] → len(arr) points. Exception: sat_fat_ratio_pct uses EXCLUSIVE upper bounds (value < arr[i] → i points; ≥ arr[-1] → len(arr)). FVL is a non-linear lookup and is given as an object. Units are per 100 g (solids) or per 100 ml (beverages), as sold.

input_derivation.energy_kj: energy_kcal × 4.184 (use a label kJ value if one is ever stored)
input_derivation.salt_g: sodium_mg × 2.5 / 1000 (EU Reg. 1169/2011 salt equivalent; the Nutri-Score update scores salt, not sodium)
input_derivation.sugars_g: TOTAL sugars (sugars_g). Never substitute added_sugars_g. If total sugars are missing, the nutrition part is 'not calculable'.
input_derivation.sat_fat_ratio_pct: fats category only: 100 × saturated_fat_g / fat_g (needs fat_g)
input_derivation.fibre_g: fiber_g; missing → 0 points (conservative; FSSAI labels often omit fibre)
input_derivation.fvl_pct: not in our data → 0 points by default (see notes.fvl)
input_derivation.non_nutritive_sweeteners: beverages only: presence in the ingredient list of E950 acesulfame-K, E951 aspartame, E952 cyclamate, E954 saccharin, E955 sucralose, E957 thaumatin, E959 neohesperidine DC, E960a steviol glycosides/stevia, E961 neotame, E962 aspartame-acesulfame salt, E969 advantame. These are the sweeteners the beverages report marks as included. Polyols (sorbitol, maltitol, xylitol, erythritol etc.) are NOT counted.
input_derivation.required_to_score: energy, sugars, saturated fat and sodium must all be present (plus fat_g for the fats category); otherwise mark nutrition as not calculable rather than guessing

general_foods.protein_rule: N = energy+sugars+sat fat+salt points. If N ≥ 11 (and the food is not cheese), score = N − (fibre + FVL), with protein NOT counted. If N < 11, score = N − (protein + fibre + FVL). Red-meat products (beef, veal, pork/swine, lamb, mutton/goat, game/venison, horse, donkey, camel, kangaroo) count at most 2 protein points. For our 'meat' category, apply the cap when the product/ingredients name one of those; chicken, fish and egg are uncapped. Since 2022 the old exception 'protein counts at N≥11 if FVL points = 5' no longer exists.
general_foods.score_range: official −17..55; with FVL fixed at 0 the practical minimum is −12
general_foods.category_notes: Powders (health_drink, kids_nutrition_drink, glucose_powder, cocoa_powder, dairy_whitener) are scored per 100 g as sold, because that is what our label data is. The beverages report says cocoa/malt drink mixes should be scored as beverages ONLY if the label gives nutrition per 100 ml as reconstituted. If a product has 'as consumed' per-100 ml data, use the beverages algorithm instead. Instant noodles: as sold. Chocolate and dark chocolate stay in general foods (cocoa products are not in the fats category). Curd (set dahi) is a solid dairy food → general. Lassi/chaas/drinking yoghurt → beverages. Honey and jaggery are scored (they will mostly be D/E); the FSSAI INR draft exempted sweeteners entirely, which is a defensible alternative if you prefer not to grade sugars.

cheese.protein_rule: Protein is ALWAYS counted (score = N − (protein + fibre + FVL)), whatever N is. Paneer is a fresh/unripened acid-coagulated cheese (Codex 1.6; WHO SEARO lists paneer under 'Cheese and analogues'), so it gets the cheese rule.

fats_oils_nuts_seeds.definition: Plant or animal fats and oils, including cream, margarines, butters and oils; plus nuts (HS 0801, 0802), processed nuts (HS 2008 11 = prepared groundnuts, which covers peanut butter, and 2008 19), groundnuts (HS 1202) and seeds (HS 1204 linseed, 1206 sunflower, 1207 other oil seeds). Chestnuts are excluded.
fats_oils_nuts_seeds.negative_notes: energy_from_saturates_kj = saturated_fat_g × 37 and replaces energy. sat_fat_ratio_pct = 100 × sat fat / total fat (EXCLUSIVE bounds: <10 → 0 … <64 → 9, ≥64 → 10) and replaces saturated fat g. Sugars and salt are as in general foods.
fats_oils_nuts_seeds.protein_rule: If N ≥ 7: score = N − (fibre + FVL), protein not counted. If N < 7: score = N − (protein + fibre + FVL). In this category FVL also counts oils made from listed fruits/vegetables (e.g. olive, avocado). Nuts are no longer FVL in either algorithm.
fats_oils_nuts_seeds.category_notes: Expected Indian results, as illustrations computed by us and not published values: ghee, butter, coconut oil, palm oil and vanaspati land in E or D (high sat-fat ratio and energy from saturates). Mustard, groundnut, rice-bran and sunflower oils land around B–C. Olive oil can reach B. Plain nuts usually score B–C. Oil FVL can be set to 5 only for olive/avocado oil, from the product name.

applies_to: health_drink / kids_nutrition_drink / tea / coffee ONLY when the record is a ready-to-drink liquid or has per-100 ml 'as consumed' data
beverages.definition: All non-alcoholic drinks: water and water-based drinks (sugar- or NNS-sweetened, flavoured), fruit/vegetable juices and nectars (incl. coconut water drinks), smoothies, coffee/tea/infusions, plain milk, milk-based drinks (flavoured, sweetened, NNS), fermented milk drinks (drinking yoghurt, kefir, buttermilk, lassi), and plant-based drinks (soy, almond, oat, rice…). Culinary coconut milk is excluded. Drinks with more than 1.2% alcohol are out of scope.
beverages.protein_rule: No cap: score = N − (protein + fibre + FVL) always.
beverages.category_notes: Since the 2023 update, milk and milk drinks are scored as beverages (before, they used the general algorithm). Units are per 100 ml. If a milk/juice label gives per 100 g, use it as is (density ≈1). For juice, FVL matters a lot: a 100% juice gets 6 FVL points, and leaving them out pushes it about two letters down (see notes.fvl).

not_scored.why: Food/health supplements. They are outside the scope of every model: the WHO SEARO model excludes 'food supplements' (§2.2.9), the FSSAI INR draft exempted category 13 (incl. 13.6 food supplements), and Nutri-Score covers foods carrying an EU 1169/2011 nutrition declaration, which excludes supplements (Directive 2002/46/EC). Per-100 g scoring of capsules or scoops is meaningless. sea_buckthorn_oil is sold mostly as a supplement; score it as fats only if it is a culinary oil.

In India these are sold as health supplements/nutraceuticals or foods for special dietary use. The FSSAI INR draft exempted 12.10 'protein products' and category 13. They are eaten in 30–100 g scoops mixed into liquid, so per-100 g-as-sold Nutri-Score results mislead (whey isolate would get A/B purely from protein). Ready-to-eat protein foods (protein_bar, protein_chip, protein_milkshake) ARE scored.

Excluded by every model (WHO SEARO §2.2.9–10, FSSAI INR Schedule IV 13.1/13.2, Nutri-Score scope excludes infant/young-child foods under EU Reg. 609/2013). Its composition is set by regulation, not by healthy-diet goals.

Exempt from mandatory nutrition declaration under EU 1169/2011 Annex V (salt, herbs, spices, vinegars), so they are outside Nutri-Score. The FSSAI INR draft exempted 12.1 salt, 12.2 herbs/spices/masalas and 12.3 vinegars. Nutrition is not the relevant question for these; contamination and adulteration are.

Plain tea leaves and coffee powder are Annex V exempt and essentially nutrient-free as consumed. Per-100 g dry values (e.g. instant coffee's protein) would mislead. Exception: score 3-in-1 premixes or ready-to-drink iced tea/coffee. Use beverages if the data is per 100 ml as consumed, otherwise general foods per 100 g as sold.

to_0_100: Use a piecewise-linear map inside each letter band, so the 0–100 number always matches the Nutri-Score letter AND OpenLabel's own letter thresholds (A ≥85, B ≥70, C ≥55, D ≥40, E <40). For a final Nutri-Score point total p in band [lo, hi] mapped to score range [s_lo, s_hi]: score = s_hi − (p − lo) × (s_hi − s_lo) / (hi − lo), clamped to the band, then rounded to an integer. Bands: GENERAL & CHEESE: A p∈[−17, 0] → [100, 85]; B [1, 2] → [84, 70]; C [3, 10] → [69, 55]; D [11, 18] → [54, 40]; E [19, 40] → [39, 0] (p > 40 → 0). FATS/OILS/NUTS/SEEDS: A [−17, −6] → [100, 85]; B [−5, 2] → [84, 70]; C [3, 10] → [69, 55]; D [11, 18] → [54, 40]; E [19, 40] → [39, 0]. BEVERAGES: A is water only (→ 100; we don't test water); B [−18, 2] → [84, 70]; C [3, 6] → [69, 55]; D [7, 9] → [54, 40]; E [10, 30] → [39, 0] (p > 30 → 0). So no drink except water can exceed 84, which mirrors Nutri-Score's rule. Examples: general p = 0 → 85, p = 2 → 70, p = 10 → 55, p = 18 → 40, p = 25 → 28. Show the Nutri-Score letter itself alongside the number.
fssai_inr_status: DRAFT ONLY; never notified, and in practice superseded. Draft FSS (Labelling and Display) Amendment Regulations, 2022 (F. No. Std./SP-08/T(FoPNL-N-01), dated 13 Sep 2022, uploaded 20 Sep 2022, comments until 28 Nov 2022; WTO G/SPS/N/IND/288) proposed the 'Indian Nutrition Rating'. It gave ½–5 stars, was HSR-style, and offered 48 months of voluntary compliance after final notification. Algorithm (Schedule III): baseline points per 100 g for solids (energy kcal ≤80 → 0 then +1 per 80 kcal to >800 → 10; sat fat 1 g steps to 10 g, then 2 g steps to >40 g → 25; total sugars 4.2 g steps to >84 g → 20; sodium 90 mg steps to >2250 mg → 25). For liquids per 100 ml, only energy (6 kcal steps → 10) and total sugars (0.1 then 1.5 g steps → 10). Positive points: FV% and NLM% (≤10 → 0, >10 → 1, then 5-point steps to >55 → 10); fibre (3 g steps to >30 g → 10); protein (≤1.5 → 0, >1.5, >2.0, >2.5, >3.0, >5, >7, >10, then 5 g steps to >50 g → 15). Caps: if baseline ≤20, up to 15 protein and 10 each FV/NLM/fibre; if >20, up to 7 protein and 5 each. Final = baseline − (FV + NLM + P + F). Stars for solids: ≤−11 → 5; −10..−7 → 4.5; −6..−2 → 4; −1..2 → 3.5; 3..6 → 3; 7..11 → 2.5; 12..15 → 2; 16..20 → 1.5; 21..24 → 1; ≥25 → 0.5. Liquids: ≤0 → 5 … ≥20 → 0.5. Schedule IV exempted milk/plain dairy, ghee/oils, fresh produce, flours/grains, sweeteners incl. honey, salt/spices, eggs, fresh meat/fish, supplements, infant foods, water and alcohol. The same draft defined HFSS as sugar energy ≥10% of total energy, OR sat-fat energy ≥10%, OR sodium ≥1 mg/kcal. Status timeline: ~14,000 comments; expert committee formed 17 Feb 2023. Supreme Court, 3S and Our Health Society v. Union of India, W.P.(C) 437/2024: the order of 9 Apr 2025 directed the expert committee to report within 3 months. FSSAI's compliance affidavit of 30 Jan 2026 said the committee found 'no consensus among the stakeholders on INR format' and proposed more research. On 10 Feb 2026 (MA 1177/2025) the Court was 'not satisfied' and asked FSSAI to consider front-of-pack WARNING labels within 4 weeks. Separately, the Draft FSS (Labelling & Display) Amendment Regulations, 2025 (17 Feb 2025; bold nutrition information) were deferred by the Food Authority on 24 Nov 2025. Per press reports (Aug–Sep 2026; not yet primary-verified): FSSAI now proposes a single-phase warning label (a Canada-style hexagon flagging high added sugar, fat or salt, with thresholds said to draw on the ICMR-NIN Dietary Guidelines for Indians 2024, plus a non-caloric-sweetener warning), with ~4 months of drafting and 365 days of voluntary compliance. The Supreme Court (Pardiwala J.) reserved its order on 28 Sep 2026. No pronouncement found as of 7 Nov 2026. Bottom line: there is no final FSSAI nutrition-rating algorithm to implement. The likely Indian direction is warning thresholds, not a graded score.
who_searo_summary: WHO Nutrient Profile Model for South-East Asia Region (WHO SEARO, © 2017; developed at a 2016 regional workshop; adapted from the WPRO/EURO models, with thresholds based on WHO population nutrient intake goals). Purpose: to classify foods for implementing WHA63.14 recommendations on marketing foods and non-alcoholic beverages to children (children >36 months). It could be adapted for taxes or school food after testing. It is PASS/FAIL, not graded: a product 'cannot be marketed if any one of the nutrients are above the threshold' per 100 g/ml as sold, or as reconstituted. General exclusions (marketing never allowed): industrial trans fat >1% of energy, alcohol >0.5% of energy, any added non-sugar sweetener. 18 categories with thresholds per 100 g (fat g / sat fat g / total sugars g / added sugars g / sodium g / kcal; '–' = none): 1 Confectionery 8/–/6/–/–/230; 2 Fine bakery wares (biscuits, cakes) 8/–/6/–/0.25/230; 3 Bread & ordinary bakery 8/–/6/–/0.25/–; 4 Cereals (incl. breakfast cereals, muesli, granola, cereal bars) 12/–/9/–/0.35/–; 5a Savoury snacks (namkeen, chips, papad) 8/–/–/0/0.25/230; 5b Processed nuts –/–/–/0/0.05/–; 5c Fish-based snacks –/–/6/–/0.25/230; 6a Juices –/–/6/0/–/–; 6b Milk & dairy drinks 7/–/–/0/–/–; 6c Water-based flavoured drinks –/–/2/–/0.30/–; 6d Coffee/tea –/–/2/–/–/–; 6e Cereal/nut/soy drinks –/–/6/–/0.20/–; 7 Frozen dairy desserts/ice cream 8/–/12/–/0.10/230; 8 Curded dairy desserts (incl. khoa, peda, burfee, gulab jamun) 7/–/6/–/0.10/230; 9 Cheese & analogues (incl. paneer) 20/–/–/0/0.60/–; 10 Composite foods (ready meals, instant noodles, soups) 8/3.5/9/–/0.35/–; 11 Fats & oils incl. ghee, butter –/35/–/–/0.10/–; 12 Pasta & noodles (as cooked) 3/–/–/–/0.25/–; 13 Fresh meat/fish 15/–/–/–/–/–; 14a Processed meat 8/–/–/–/0.40/–; 14b Processed fish 8/3/–/–/0.40/–; 15 Fresh fruit/veg/legumes/nuts: permitted; 16 Processed fruit & veg (jam, pickles, peanut butter) –/–/–/0/0.40/–; 17 Soy products (tofu, soya chunks) 12/–/5/0/0.10/–; 18 Sauces, dips, dressings (ketchup, chutney) 12/–/10/–/0.30/–. Use in OpenLabel: an India-relevant secondary flag ('would not be permitted for marketing to children under the WHO SEARO model: exceeds sugar threshold'), not a score. India is a SEAR member state, and the FSSAI expert panel reportedly drew INR thresholds from this model. Caveat: added-sugar thresholds of 0 mean ANY added sugar fails. Our added_sugars_g is often missing, so evaluate that criterion only when present, or from the ingredients list.
health_star_rating_summary: Australia/NZ Health Star Rating (government-led and voluntary; current document 'HSR System Implementation Guide' v9, Dec 2025, which restructures v8/Calculator & Style Guide v8.1 of Jun 2025 with no policy change). Six categories: 1 non-dairy beverages (and jellies, water ices); 1D milk & dairy beverages (and alternatives); 2 foods; 2D dairy foods; 3 oils & spreads; 3D cheese. HSR score = baseline points (energy kJ, saturated fat, total sugars, sodium per 100 g/ml) − modifying points (V = fruit/veg/nut/legume %, P = protein, F = fibre). The score is converted to ½–5 stars with a category-specific conversion table. Like the 2017 Nutri-Score (from the same UK FSA/Ofcom lineage), protein points are restricted for high-baseline foods unless FVNL is high. NOT verified from the primary PDF: the healthstarrating.gov.au PDFs timed out, so the exact point tables and protein-restriction thresholds were not checked and are deliberately omitted here.

notes.fvl: We have no FVL%. Default it to 0 points. That is conservative (it can only make a grade worse, never better), and since 2022 it no longer affects whether protein is counted. It mainly penalises fruit juices, fruit/veg-based products, pulse-based foods, and olive/avocado oil. Optional, clearly labelled refinement: estimate FVL only from an explicit percentage declared in the ingredients text (e.g. 'mango pulp (35%)', 'tomato paste (28%)'), summing fruits, vegetables and pulses/legumes (NOT nuts, NOT millets, NOT cereals). Also, juice whose name or ingredients say '100% juice' / 'no added sugar' with a single fruit ingredient can take FVL >80%. Show 'fruit/veg content not measured – scored as 0' in the explanation. Example from our own calculation: a 100% orange juice at ~190 kJ, 9 g sugar per 100 ml gets N = 3 + 7 = 10. That is E without FVL, but 10 − 6 = 4 → C with FVL — a two-letter swing. So the juice estimate is worth doing.
notes.fibre: Indian labels often don't declare fibre. Missing → 0 points (conservative); say so in the explanation. Whole-grain atta, muesli and oats will be under-rated when fibre is missing.
notes.sugars: Nutri-Score uses TOTAL sugars, so plain milk, curd and fruit juices are penalised for intrinsic sugars by design. Use added_sugars_g only for the WHO SEARO/FSSAI HFSS side-flags, never inside Nutri-Score.
notes.trans_fat: None of the graded models score trans fat. Keep it in the safety part (FSSAI limit: industrial TFA ≤2% of total fat in fats/oils and in foods containing them). WHO SEARO's >1%-of-energy industrial-TFA rule can be part of the WHO flag.
notes.as_sold_vs_prepared: Score per 100 g/ml as sold (our data). Nutri-Score and WHO SEARO prefer 'as reconstituted' for powders, soups, noodles and drink mixes only when the label gives such values. Flag powders in the explanation.
notes.dairy_beverage_boundary: milk, protein_milkshake, lassi/chaas/flavoured milk → beverages (2023 rule). curd/dahi, paneer, cheese, ice cream → solids.
notes.india_caveat: Nutri-Score was calibrated on French/German/Dutch/Belgian/Spanish food databases and European dietary guidelines. Indian products (namkeen, mithai, ghee, batters) were not part of the calibration. It is not recognised by FSSAI. Present it as 'Nutri-Score (European public-health algorithm, 2023 update) applied to the pack's nutrition values'. Show the WHO SEARO marketing-to-children check and the FSSAI-draft HFSS check (sugar energy ≥10%, sat-fat energy ≥10%, sodium ≥1 mg/kcal) as India-relevant badges. When FSSAI finalises warning-label thresholds, add them as a badge too.
notes.versus_current_grade: Current backend/grading.py uses 2017 thresholds (sugars in 4.5 g steps up to 10 points; sodium in 90 mg steps) and one algorithm for everything. Changes needed: salt-based 20-point scale, 15-point sugar scale, the 2022 protein rule (cheese exception only, red-meat cap 2), a separate fats algorithm, and a separate beverages algorithm with NNS points and its own letter cut-offs.
